name: NVIDIA H100 SXM5 80GB (GH100, compute capability 9.0)
notes: Published figures, not a measurement: no device run has confirmed any of them, and none has run here. launch_ns, link_ns, memory_efficiency, occupancy_to_saturate and memory_latency_ns are assumptions, the same on every packaged card, marked as such below.

documents.whitepaper: NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPU Architecture whitepaper, Table 3, the H100 SXM5 column (https://resources.nvidia.com/en-us-hopper-architecture/nvidia-h100-tensor-c)
documents.product_page: NVIDIA H100 product specifications, the H100 SXM column (https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/h100/)
documents.guide: CUDA Programming Guide 13.4.2, Compute Capabilities, Tables 30 and 31 (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html)

source.sms: Hopper whitepaper: 132 SMs of 128 FP32 cores and 64 INT32 cores each; GPU boost clock 1980 MHz for FP32, FP64 and FP64 tensor operations, 1830 MHz for FP8, FP16, BF16 and TF32 tensor operations. ghz is the 1980 MHz clock; the tensor figures below already carry the lower one.
source.dram_gbps: Hopper whitepaper: memory bandwidth 3352 GB/s (HBM3); the product page rounds it to 3.35 TB/s.
source.flops: Hopper whitepaper: Peak FP32 66.9 TFLOPS, Peak FP64 33.5 TFLOPS, Peak INT32 TOPS 33.5 (64 INT32 cores an SM, 2 operations each a clock, the convention every packaged card follows). The product page rounds them to 67 and 34.
source.tensor: Hopper whitepaper, dense (the sparse figures are twice these): TF32 494.7, FP16 and BF16 with FP32 accumulate 989.4, FP8 with FP32 accumulate 1978.9 TFLOPS. The model reads tensor_f16; the others are recorded for a reader.
source.link_gbps: Product page: PCIe Gen5 128 GB/s, both directions together, so 64 GB/s each way, before protocol overhead. NVLink joins GPUs to each other, not to the host.
source.occupancy: CUDA Programming Guide 13.4.2, Compute Capabilities, Tables 30 and 31 (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html), 9.0 column: 64 K registers, 64 warps (2048 threads) and 228 KB of shared memory an SM; the CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9, section 20, says for each of 8.x, 9.0, 10.x and 12.0 that the 1 KB of shared memory not made available to a thread block is reserved for system use (shared_reserved); the CUDA Occupancy Calculator allocates registers a warp at a time in units of 256 (register_unit). No limit on resident blocks per SM is applied here.
source.shared_bytes_per_clock: CUDA C++ Programming Guide: shared memory has 32 banks, each 32 bits wide a clock cycle.
source.memory_latency_ns: Assumed. NVIDIA publishes no device-memory latency and no run here has measured one; it prices only a pipeline's asynchronous copies, as the bytes in flight over this latency. Every packaged card assumes the same 500 ns.
